data.cultural_impact: The name Imaran can be considered as a reflection of the deep reverence for the divine in Hindu culture. By invoking the name of the god as a dwelling place, it is a reminder of the belief that the divine is always present in our lives and surroundings.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Imaran holds the belief that the divine presence is the ultimate abode, a place of refuge and solace. It serves as a constant reminder that God is always with us, guiding and protecting us. The name also holds the significance of seeking refuge and stability in the divine presence.

historical_references.reference: Imaran is mentioned as a ruler of Malwa (central India) in the 12th century A.D. during the reign of Prithviraj Chauhan. He is described as a vassal of the Chauhan king and a powerful warrior.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Chauhan Dynasty, Prithviraj Chauhan's reign

historical_references.reference: Imaran is also mentioned in the 13th-century Persian text 'Tarikh-i-Masudi' as the founder of the town of Sagar in Madhya Pradesh, India. He is described as a Hindu Raja and a generous patron of learning and arts.
